page.layout: Running head across the top: "Primus Index". Left column, full height of this part: alphabetical index of entries in italic with page references. Right column at the top only: a letter "I", then a Greek entry, then short index lines beside the left column.; One column of alphabetical index on the right half of the page, lines running from top to bottom; below the last line, at the far right, the catchword "de".

main_text.l: Homerus descriptiones morum, posteris primum patefecit. 91.11
de homine aliter sentiente, aliter loquente. 107.23
Horatij locus de morum in hominibus observatione. 93.6

page.notes: The Greek entries at the top right are not legible on the scan; they are marked illegible rather than guessed. The right column's first Greek line is a large initial letter, so its first letter is uncertain. Page references after the Hieronymi and Horatij lines are read as printed; the dotted numbers are given as they appear. Long s is rendered as plain s throughout. Uncertain readings: "cuussa" (hyphen-joined line, possibly a different word), "fictis" in the entry "de fictis amicis". Long s is rendered as s throughout (for example "Isaus", "Isocratis", "causidico", "se"), and u/v follows the vowel/consonant rule. The top of the page is not visible on this part, so no running head or page number is given.
